entitySubtype: Peer-Reviewed Scientific Article / Machine Learning and Historical Astronomical Plates
name: Use of machine learning to enhance detection of transient astronomical phenomena in historical observatory images
summary: Peer-reviewed Scientific Reports study training a supervised classifier on 250 expert-labeled transient image pairs and applying it to 107,875 previously identified candidates. The authors report that nuclear-window and Earth-shadow patterns persist after model-based artifact control, while the physical nature of the candidates remains unresolved.

relationships.role: research context; not an established detection

researchLibraryMetadata.methodology: Supervised machine-learning classifier trained on 250 expert-reviewed paired plate candidates, evaluated with five-fold out-of-fold performance, then deployed across 107,875 previously identified transient candidates.
researchLibraryMetadata.principalFindings: Reported AUC 0.81, sensitivity 0.71 and specificity 0.71; the authors report persistent nuclear-window and Earth-shadow patterns after probability-based artifact control.
researchLibraryMetadata.limitations: Small expert-labeled training set relative to deployment data, imperfect classification, possible label and dataset biases, and no physical identification of the candidates.
researchLibraryMetadata.researchImplication: The study adds peer-reviewed ensemble-level evidence to the VASCO debate but does not establish technosignatures or extraterrestrial technology.

editorialNotes.debatePosition: Preserve alongside, not over, the original VASCO studies and Watters et al. critique.
editorialNotes.probabilityBoundary: Model probability of a real transient is not probability of artificial or extraterrestrial origin.
editorialNotes.lifecyclePrinciple: News can age; knowledge does not.
